📌 Farm Fund low-interest secured loan fund — The Co-op set up a low-interest secured loan fund for farm infrastructure in partnership with Industrial Credit Union and the Whatcom Community Foundation. Source: communityfood.coop Farm Fund history. kind: Money — grant or loan fund direction: two-way

text.tspan: Farm Fund low-interest secured loan fund

g.title: 📌 Farm Fund grant — co-op development for farmworkers — Listed in the Farm Fund's earlier projects: funded Community to Community's work "on cooperative development for farm workers and Latino consumer access to local food". Year not given. kind: Money — grant or loan fund

📌 Organised and incubated the co-op; led the land fundraising — C2C organised Washington's first farmworker-owned co-op farm and raised grants, public funds and private donations to buy the 65 acres; the land is meant to pass to a land trust. Source: PCC Sound Consumer, June 2023. kind: Built or helped build the co-op
📌 Supplies produce — The Bellingham food co-op is among Tierra y Libertad's buyers. Source: PCC Sound Consumer, June 2023. kind: Trade — supplies goods

📌 Supplies grass-fed beef — The Co-op stocks North Cascade Meats beef (Barrau Farms, Whatcom; Forest Cattle Co., Skagit). The Co-op's general manager and meat manager took part in launching the meat co-op, and the Farm Fund paid for a Matheson Farms field day (2016–19) that covered "benefits of the cooperative model" — Matheson is a founding board farm. kind: Trade — supplies goods

📌 Co-op development help (USDA grant) — Technical assistance under a USDA Rural Cooperative Development Grant, including the securities exemptions that let the co-op sell membership and equity shares. Source: agbizcenter.org. kind: Built or helped build the co-op
📌 Incubated the food hub — NABC ran the hub until it incorporated as a farmer-owned co-op in 2016 and governance passed to its own board. kind: Built or helped build the co-op
📌 Home-care co-op support — NWCDC lists Circle of Life among the Washington home-care co-ops it serves. Its role in the 2009 founding is not documented. kind: Built or helped build the co-op

📌 Network of co-ops in Whatcom and Skagit counties, began 2014 as the Co-op Education Project, renamed 2019, incorporated as a secondary co-op in January 2022. No fixed office — pin is downtown Bellingham. cascadecooperatives.coop · (360) 441-2728. Its Google map of Whatcom & Skagit co-ops is the main source for this layer. lat: 48.7474 lng: -122.476 kind: Co-op network mapId: cc _onMap: http://localhost:8765/maps/rcn_map.html?lat=48.7474&lng=-122.476&zoom=16&openissue=whatcom-wa--cooperatives website: http://cascadecooperatives.coop phone: (360) 441-2728 email: cascadecooperatives@gmail.com contactCaveat: Site’s https certificate is broken — use the http:// address contactChecked: Sep 2026 contactSource: cascadecooperatives.coop About page people: Alyssa Young — Board Director (Cascade Mountain Ascents)

📌 1319 Cornwall Ave, Suite 101, Bellingham (moved from 203 W Holly St; Mount Vernon office too). Founded 2003 by Rosalinda Guillén.
